primitives.name: Talent Evaluation Inference
primitives.verbatim_quote: This paper examines this problem by analyzing which skills translate to the NBA game, dissecting what NBA executives value when selecting international players, and by analyzing which international statistics and characteristics are significant determinants of success in the NBA.
primitives.assumptions: Executive evaluations are based on quantifiable statistical proxies and historical performance trends.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When statistical proxies fail to capture cultural or physical adaptation factors.

layer2.mapping: Maps executive decision-making to probabilistic forecasting of player performance using historical regression models.
layer2.telemetry: Draft selection consistency vs. post-draft performance variance.

primitives.name: International Player Compatibility
primitives.verbatim_quote: Notable early draft selections, such as the Pistons' pick of Darko Milicic, indicate that the league may still have much to learn about what makes an international player compatible with the NBA and successful in the league.
primitives.assumptions: Compatibility is a latent variable dependent on training, cultural fit, and physical attributes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When cultural or physiological mismatches occur despite strong statistical indicators.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphism between international player traits and NBA performance outcomes through structured scouting protocols.
layer2.telemetry: Post-draft minutes played and role assignment accuracy.

primitives.name: Draft Selection Outcomes
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Houston Rockets picked Yao Ming with the first pick in 2002 while the Detroit Pistons selected Darko Milicic with the second pick in 2003.
primitives.assumptions: Draft picks are made under uncertainty with imperfect information about future performance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When high-value picks underperform due to misalignment of expectations and actual outcomes.

layer2.mapping: Derives expected utility of draft picks from comparative analysis of past selections and their long-term impact.
layer2.telemetry: Number of years played, average minutes per game, and salary-adjusted performance metrics.

The 'International Player Compatibility' primitive introduces a latent variable model where compatibility is inferred from observable traits and past outcomes.
